summary: Follow-up part for GN.5, Certified reductions and applications, continuing the accepted parent packet's 24 LLL nodes, which are cited by id. It reconciles Lenstra–Lenstra–Lovász Algorithm (1.15) with the native full-row variant by planning one nondeterministic step relation whose invariant (1.16)–(1.17), termination and swap count are proved once, both algorithms being refinements that run in lockstep away from exact ties; it plans Proposition (1.26) (O(n⁴ log B) operations on integers of length O(n log B)) with the denominator integrality (1.27)–(1.29) and size bounds (1.30)–(1.36), and the bounds (1.7)–(1.14) relating a reduced basis to the covolume, independent vectors and successive minima; it supplies the routed primitive-prefix basis with explicit constants; it moves the generic Fincke–Pohst enumeration down from EffectiveDiophantineMethods ED.1, with completeness, lattice-point counts and certified representation numbers of Tau Ceti integral lattices; it transfers reduction and enumeration to irrational metrics through a certified Loewner comparison with a rational model; and it states the number-field adapters (Euclidean ideal lattice, house, norm and height bounds, certified short elements and class representatives, simultaneous approximation (1.39)) and the arithmetic-group adapters (LLL-reduced forms are Siegel-reduced in the sense of AdelicAlgebraicGroups AA.3, and an LLL certificate places GL_n(ℝ) in an explicit standard Siegel domain).
conventions: Indices are zero based: the cursor k means the prefix b_0, …, b_{k−1} is checked; the source's one-based (1.15) subscript is k + 1. Nodes stated with the source's indexing say so.
δ = 3/4; the Lovász test is strict; nearest integers are Mathlib's round, ⌊t + 1/2⌋, unless a node names another tie rule.
d_k = det Gram(b_0, …, b_{k−1}), d_0 = 1, and D = ∏_{1≤k<n} d_k as in the parent's integer potential.
Number fields use Mathlib's Euclidean mixed space, which counts each complex place once; the trace form is not used as a metric here.
Siegel domains follow AdelicAlgebraicGroups AA.3: left GL_n(ℤ)-action, coordinates v·diag(a)·k, gram g = (g^{−1})ᵀg^{−1}.

nodes.title: The LLL step relation at δ = 3/4
nodes.statement: Fix a real inner-product space E and n ≥ 2. A state is a pair (k, b) of a cursor 1 ≤ k ≤ n and a linearly independent family b : Fin n → E (zero-based; the prefix b_0, …, b_{k−1} has been checked and row k is current). For k < n the relation (k, b) ⟶ (k′, c) holds when c arises from b in two moves. Size move: b′ agrees with b except b′_k = b_k − Σ_{l<k} r_l b_l for integers r_l, chosen so that the new coefficient satisfies |μ(b′)_{k,k−1}| ≤ 1/2; the integers r_l for l < k − 1 are unconstrained. Decision: if ‖b′*_k‖² < (3/4 − μ(b′)²_{k,k−1})·‖b′*_{k−1}‖² (Case 1, the strict Lovász failure), c is b′ with entries k − 1 and k interchanged and k′ = max(1, k − 1); otherwise (Case 2), c arises from b′ by further integer shears of row k by rows l < k with |μ(c)_{k,l}| ≤ 1/2 for every l < k, and k′ = k + 1. Here b* is Mathlib's ordered gramSchmidt and μ is the parent coefficient lllCoefficient. States with k = n are terminal. In ranks 0 and 1 the unique state is terminal.
hypotheses: Zero-based cursor: the source's one-based subscript k ∈ {2, …, n+1} of (1.15) is our k + 1; its start k = 2 is our k = 1 and its stop k = n + 1 is our k = n.

The relation fixes no tie rule for nearest integers and allows any extra shears of row k by earlier rows before the test: Algorithm (1.15) and the native full-row variant are deterministic refinements of it.
Comparisons are decided exactly in ℚ when the Gram matrix of b is rational; δ = 3/4 throughout.
proofSteps: Package the size move as an integer upper-unitriangular change of the current row, the Case 1 move as the adjacent transposition, and the Case 2 move as further row-k shears.
Express each move by the parent shear and swap certificates, so the relation carries a unimodular certificate from the input.
Record the coefficient and Gram–Schmidt updates of each move from the parent shear and swap update lemmas.
acceptance: On ((2,0),(0,1)) at cursor 1 the only step is the swap to ((0,1),(2,0)) with cursor 1.
The family with Gram matrix [[1,1/2],[1/2,3/4]] satisfies the Lovász inequality with equality, so its only step is Case 2.

sources.match: The algorithm keeps a current subscript, first achieves |μ_{k,k−1}| ≤ 1/2 by one shear, swaps and moves the subscript down when the strict Lovász test (1.19) fails, and otherwise reduces the remaining coefficients of row k and moves up; the nondeterministic relation abstracts exactly these moves.
The figure fixes the order of the moves that the relation allows.

nodes.title: The invariant (1.16)–(1.17) and prefix reducedness
nodes.statement: Write Inv(k, b) for: |μ_{ij}| ≤ 1/2 for j < i < k, and ‖b*_i‖² ≥ (3/4 − μ²_{i,i−1})·‖b*_{i−1}‖² for 1 ≤ i < k. Then Inv(1, b) holds for every independent b; if Inv(k, b) and (k, b) ⟶ (k′, c) then Inv(k′, c) and span_ℤ(c) = span_ℤ(b); a terminal state (n, b) with Inv(n, b) is LLL-reduced. Moreover, along any chain from (1, b), the first time the cursor reaches m (1 ≤ m ≤ n), the vectors c_0, …, c_{m−1} form an LLL-reduced basis of the lattice spanned by the first m input vectors.
hypotheses: The last statement is Remark (1.37) of the source in zero-based form.
No integrality of the Gram data is needed for this lemma.
proofSteps: Case 2: the size move and the further shears only change row k by earlier rows, so all Gram–Schmidt vectors and the coefficients of rows i < k are unchanged; the strict Lovász test failed to fire, so Inv extends to k + 1.
Case 1: the swap only changes b*_{k−1}, b*_k and coefficients in rows ≥ k − 1; the prefix below k − 1 is untouched, so Inv(max(1, k − 1), c) holds.
Terminal: Inv(n, b) is exactly the size and adjacent Lovász conditions of the parent IsLLLReduced, with independence preserved by the certificate.
Prefix statement: before the cursor first reaches m, no step touches rows ≥ m, and every move inside the prefix preserves the ℤ-span of its first m vectors.
acceptance: On ((2,0),(0,1)) the chain (1, b) ⟶ (1, ((0,1),(2,0))) ⟶ (2, ((0,1),(2,0))) satisfies Inv at every state and ends LLL-reduced.
After the first time the cursor reaches 1 nothing is asserted beyond the first vector; Inv(1, b) is vacuous.

nodes.title: Termination and swap count of LLL reduction
nodes.statement: (a) Integral data. Let b be independent with integral Gram matrix (a rational Gram matrix is first scaled by a common denominator, which changes no decision). Along any chain of the step relation from (1, b), Case 1 occurs at most log_{4/3} D(b) times, where D(b) = ∏_{i=1}^{n−1} d_i(b) is the parent integer potential, and Case 2 occurs at most (number of Case 1 steps) + n − 1 times; every chain is finite and has at most n − 1 + 2·log_{4/3} D(b) steps. If ‖b_i‖² ≤ B for all i, with B ≥ 1, then d_i(b) ≤ B^i and D(b) ≤ B^{n(n−1)/2}, so at most (n(n−1)/2)·log_{4/3} B swaps occur. (b) Real data. For an arbitrary lattice L in E with independent basis b, every chain is still finite: along a chain each d_i is at least (2^{−i}·vol(B_i)·m(L)^{i/2})², where B_i is the closed unit ball of dimension i and m(L) the minimum of ‖x‖² over nonzero x ∈ L, so D is bounded below by a positive constant depending only on L, and each swap multiplies D by less than 3/4.
hypotheses: Swap counts are counts of Case 1 steps, independent of the tie rule and of extra shears.
The lower bound in (b) replaces the source's Hermite-constant bound (3/4)^{i(i−1)/2} m(L)^i by Minkowski's first theorem; only positivity is used.
proofSteps: Shears leave every d_i unchanged (parent lll-prefix-shear-invariant); a Case 1 step replaces d_k by a factor T/B < 3/4 of itself and leaves the others (parent lll-prefix-swap-ratio, lll-strict-potential-decrease).
In (a) D is a positive integer (parent lll-prefix-gram-integral), so it is at least 1 and decreases by a factor below 3/4 at each swap: at most log_{4/3} D(b) swaps.
The cursor starts at 1, ends at n, falls by at most 1 in Case 1 and rises by 1 in Case 2, which bounds the Case 2 steps.
d_i = ∏_{l<i} ‖b*_l‖² ≤ ∏_{l<i} ‖b_l‖² ≤ B^i by the Gram–Schmidt product formula and Hadamard's inequality.

In (b), d_i is the squared covolume of the rank-i lattice spanned by b_0, …, b_{i−1} in its real span; Minkowski's first theorem in that span gives a nonzero lattice vector of squared length at most 4·(d_i^{1/2}/vol(B_i))^{2/i}, whence the lower bound.
acceptance: In rank 1 the bound is n − 1 + 0 = 0 steps.
For the identity basis B = 1 forces zero swaps.

nodes.title: Algorithm (1.15) of Lenstra–Lenstra–Lovász
nodes.statement: The deterministic reduction of Fig. 1. State: the family b together with the exact rational data μ_{ij} (j < i) and B_i = ‖b*_i‖², initialised by Gram–Schmidt and afterwards only updated, never recomputed. At cursor k < n: (1) if |μ_{k,k−1}| > 1/2, replace b_k by b_k − r·b_{k−1} with r = round(μ_{k,k−1}) (Mathlib's round, ⌊t + 1/2⌋) and update μ_{k,j} for j ≤ k − 1; (2) if B_k < (3/4 − μ²_{k,k−1})·B_{k−1}, swap b_{k−1} and b_k, update B_{k−1}, B_k and the coefficients by the formulas of (1.22), and set k := max(1, k − 1); otherwise, for l = k − 2, …, 0, if |μ_{k,l}| > 1/2 shear row k by round(μ_{k,l})·b_l, and set k := k + 1. The run starts at k = 1 and stops at k = n; it returns the final family, the composed unimodular certificate, and the number of swaps. Ranks 0 and 1 return the input with the identity certificate.
hypotheses: A coefficient equal to ±1/2 is left alone, as in the source's (*), which only acts when |μ| > 1/2.
Termination is the step-relation termination for integral or rational Gram data.
proofSteps: Each source step is a step of the relation: the shear of (1) gives |μ_{k,k−1}| ≤ 1/2 by abs_sub_round, the test is the strict Lovász test, and Case 2 ends with all |μ_{k,l}| ≤ 1/2.

The stored μ and B agree with lllCoefficient and the Gram–Schmidt norms of the current family after every step: the shear updates are the parent shear-coefficient lemma and the swap updates are (1.22), i.e. the parent swap lemmas.
Define the run by well-founded recursion on the lexicographic measure of the termination theorem, and read off reducedness from the invariant at k = n.
acceptance: On ((1,0),(1,1)) the run shears once with r = 1, passes the test and returns ((1,0),(0,1)) with certificate [[1,−1],[0,1]].
Every output satisfies the parent IsLLLReduced and spans the input lattice.

nodes.title: Algorithm (1.15) and the native full-row variant agree
nodes.statement: (a) Every transition of the parent native variant exactLLL (full descending nearest-integer reduction of row k, then the strict Lovász test, then swap with cursor max(1, k − 1) or advance) and every step of Algorithm (1.15) is a step of the LLL step relation. Hence both satisfy the invariant (1.16)–(1.17), both terminate within the swap bound log_{4/3} D(b) for integral Gram data, and both return LLL-reduced bases of the input lattice with unimodular certificates. (b) Run both from the same input. As long as no Case 1 step occurs at which the coefficient μ_{k,k−1}, after its size reduction, equals ±1/2, the two runs visit the same cursors, take the same decisions, have the same Gram–Schmidt vectors b*_i at every step, and their families differ by an integer upper unitriangular matrix (b′_i − b_i ∈ span_ℤ(b_0, …, b_{i−1}) for every i). (c) At such a tie the runs may diverge; part (a) still holds for both.
hypotheses: The relation of (b) is equality of the flag of ℤ-spans of prefixes; it implies equality of every Gram–Schmidt vector.
proofSteps: (a) The native size move uses round, so |μ_{k,k−1}| ≤ 1/2 after it (abs_sub_round) and the full descending reduction gives the Case 2 condition (parent lll-descending-size-reduction); the source steps are steps by lll-source-algorithm.
(b) Induction on the step count. Families related by an integer upper unitriangular matrix have the same prefix spans, hence the same Gram–Schmidt vectors (span_gramSchmidt_Iio).

Before the test the two values of μ_{k,k−1} differ by an integer (the b*_{k−1}-coordinate of an element of span_ℤ(b_0, …, b_{k−1}) is its integer coefficient on b_{k−1}); after size reduction both lie in [−1/2, 1/2], so they agree unless the pair is {−1/2, 1/2}. The Lovász test only involves μ², B_{k−1} and B_k, so the decisions agree.

With equal μ_{k,k−1}, the two current rows differ by an element of span_ℤ(b_0, …, b_{k−2}), so after the swap the families are still related by an upper unitriangular integer matrix; in Case 2 both rows are reduced in the same coset of span_ℤ(b_0, …, b_{k−1}).

(c) On ((2,0),(1,1)) the coefficient μ_{10} is 1/2 and the test fails (1 < (3/4 − 1/4)·4). Algorithm (1.15) swaps without shearing and ends at ((1,1),(1,−1)); the native variant first shears to (−1,1), swaps, and ends at ((−1,1),(1,1)). The Gram–Schmidt vectors differ, both outputs are LLL-reduced; nothing beyond (a) is asserted at ties.
acceptance: On ((2,0),(0,1)) both variants perform the same single swap and return ((0,1),(2,0)).
On ((2,0),(1,5)) the outputs differ ((1,5) against (−1,5)) but both are LLL-reduced with equal Gram–Schmidt norms 4 and 25.
On ((2,0),(1,1)) a tie precedes a swap: the outputs ((1,1),(1,−1)) and ((−1,1),(1,1)) have different Gram–Schmidt vectors, and both are LLL-reduced.

sources.match: The source reduces only μ_{k,k−1} before the Lovász test and reduces the rest of row k only on success; the native variant reduces the whole row first. The shears by earlier rows leave b*_{k−1}, b*_k and μ_{k,k−1} unchanged, which is why the decisions agree.
b*_i is the projection of b_i orthogonal to the span of b_1, …, b_{i−1}, so it depends only on the flag of prefix spans.

nodes.title: The prefix determinants are common denominators
nodes.statement: Let b : Fin n → E be independent with integral Gram matrix, and d_k = det Gram(b_0, …, b_{k−1}) for 0 ≤ k ≤ n (d_0 = 1). Then (i) ‖b*_i‖² = d_{i+1}/d_i; (ii) d_i·b*_i ∈ span_ℤ(b_0, …, b_i); (iii) d_{j+1}·μ_{ij} ∈ ℤ for j < i. In particular every Gram–Schmidt quantity the reduction stores is an integer divided by one of the positive integers d_k.
hypotheses: Zero-based indexing: the source's (1.27)–(1.29) read ‖b*_i‖² = d_i/d_{i−1}, d_{i−1}b*_i ∈ L and d_jμ_{ij} ∈ ℤ with one-based indices.
When b_i ∈ ℤ^m, (ii) gives d_i·b*_i ∈ ℤ^m.
proofSteps: (i) is the quotient of two instances of the parent prefix Gram product.
(ii) Write b*_i = b_i − Σ_{j<i} λ_{ij} b_j; the λ_{ij} solve the linear system with matrix Gram(b_0, …, b_{i−1}) and integral right-hand side (⟨b_i, b_l⟩)_l, so Cramer's rule gives d_i·λ_{ij} ∈ ℤ.
(iii) d_{j+1}μ_{ij} = d_{j+1}⟨b_i, b*_j⟩/‖b*_j‖² = ⟨b_i, d_j b*_j⟩, an integer by (ii) and integrality of the Gram matrix.
acceptance: d_0 b*_0 = b_0 always lies in the lattice.

sources.locator: §1, (1.27)–(1.29) and their proofs, reprint folio 35 (PDF p. 9)
sources.match: The d_i serve as denominators: |b*_i|² = d_i/d_{i−1}, d_{i−1}b*_i lies in L, and d_jμ_{ij} is an integer, proved by solving for the coefficients of b*_i and using (1.24).

nodes.title: Sizes of all numbers during Algorithm (1.15)
nodes.statement: In the source's one-based indexing: let b_1, …, b_n ∈ ℤ^n be a basis of L with |b_i|² ≤ B for all i, B ≥ 2, and run Algorithm (1.15). Throughout the run, d_i ≤ B^i, |b*_i|² ≤ B, |μ_{ij}| ≤ 2^{n−1}(nB^{n−1})^{1/2} for 1 ≤ j < i ≤ n, and |b_i|² ≤ n²(4B)^n. Each time the run returns to the situation (1.16)–(1.17) with current subscript k: (1.30) |b_i|² ≤ nB for i ≠ k; (1.31) |b_k|² ≤ n²(4B)^n if k ≠ n + 1; (1.32) |μ_{ij}| ≤ 1/2 for j < i < k; (1.33) |μ_{ij}| ≤ (nB^j)^{1/2} for j < i and i > k; (1.34) |μ_{kj}| ≤ 2^{n−k}(nB^{n−1})^{1/2} for j < k when k ≠ n + 1. The comparison (1.35) μ_{ij}² ≤ |b_i|²/|b*_j|² = d_{j−1}|b_i|²/d_j ≤ B^{j−1}|b_i|² links the coefficient and length bounds.
hypotheses: The bounds are stated for Algorithm (1.15); the native variant has its own constants and is not covered here.
In the zero-based notation of the packet, d_i and b*_i shift as in lll-denominator-integrality.
proofSteps: The d_i never increase (they change only in Case 1, by a factor below 3/4) and start at most B^i; max_i |b*_i|² never increases, since in (1.22) the new |c*_{k−1}|² is below 3/4 of |b*_{k−1}|² and |c*_k|² ≤ |b*_{k−1}|².
(1.30) is preserved: Case 1 does not change the set {b_i : i ≠ k}, Case 2 replaces {b_i : i > k} by a subset, and for i < k it follows from (1.32); (1.33) follows from (1.30) and (1.35).

(1.34): at the end of Case 2 it is (1.33) at the previous stage; at the end of Case 1, size reduction (1.18) replaces μ_{kj} by μ_{kj} − rμ_{k−1,j} with |r| < 2|μ_{k,k−1}|, which at most doubles the bound (1.36).
Between returns, each size-reduction pass at most doubles max_j |μ_{kj}|, giving the global coefficient bound, and |b_k|² ≤ Σ_j μ_{kj}²|b*_j|² + |b*_k|² gives the global length bound.
acceptance: For n = 2, B = 4 and b = ((2,0),(0,1)) the bounds give d_1 ≤ 4, |μ_{21}| ≤ 2·(2·4)^{1/2} and |b_i|² ≤ 4·16², all met by the run's actual values 4, 0 and 4.
In rank one every bound is the input bound |b_1|² ≤ B.

sources.locator: Proof of (1.26), inequalities (1.30)–(1.36) and the final two bounds, reprint folios 35–36 (PDF pp. 9–10)
sources.match: The source proves that d_i ≤ B^i and |b*_i|² ≤ B throughout, establishes (1.30)–(1.34) at each return to (1.16)–(1.17) using (1.35) and (1.36), and concludes |μ_{ij}| ≤ 2^{n−1}(nB^{n−1})^{1/2} and |b_i|² ≤ n²(4B)^n throughout.

nodes.title: Polynomial running time of LLL reduction (Proposition 1.26)
nodes.statement: Let L ⊂ ℤ^n be a lattice with basis b_1, …, b_n and B ≥ 2 with |b_i|² ≤ B. Algorithm (1.15), carried out on integers by storing the vectors b_i, the prefix determinants d_i and the numerators d_jμ_{ij} (one-based), needs O(n⁴ log B) arithmetic operations (addition, subtraction, multiplication and exact division of integers), and every integer on which an operation is performed has binary length O(n log B). With schoolbook integer arithmetic this is O(n⁶ (log B)³) bit operations. Formal version: for the cost-instrumented integral run, which charges one unit per integer operation, there is an absolute constant C such that the total charge is at most C·n⁴·log B, every stored integer has absolute value at most n·(4B)^{2n}, and every operand of an operation (a stored integer, or a sum of two products of stored integers before an exact division) has absolute value at most 2n²·(4B)^{4n}.
hypotheses: Rational input is first scaled to integral Gram data; the source's Remark (1.38) allows integral Gram data instead of L ⊂ ℤ^n.
The constant C is absolute; no claim is made about its value beyond existence, and no bound is claimed for floating-point variants.
proofSteps: The initialisation computes the d_i and the numerators d_jμ_{ij} in O(n³) operations (lll-denominator-integrality).
By the termination theorem with d_i ≤ B^i and D ≥ 1, Cases 1 and 2 occur O(n² log B) times.
Step (1.18) and Case 1 cost O(n) operations; Case 2 treats O(n) values of l at O(n) operations each; multiply by the number of passes.

Stored integers: d_i ≤ B^n, |d_jμ_{ij}| ≤ B^{n−1}·2^{n−1}(nB^{n−1})^{1/2}, and every coordinate of b_i is at most n(4B)^{n/2} by the size bounds; each is at most n(4B)^{2n}. The integral update formulas add two products of stored integers before an exact division, which gives the operand bound.
acceptance: For n = 1 the run performs no step after initialisation.
For B = 2 and n = 2 the swap bound is at most log_{4/3} 2 < 3 and every stored integer is at most 2·8⁴.

sources.locator: Proposition (1.26), its Remark and proof, reprint folios 34–36 (PDF pp. 8–10)
sources.match: For a lattice in ℤ^n with |b_i|² ≤ B, B ≥ 2, the algorithm needs O(n⁴ log B) arithmetic operations on integers of binary length O(n log B), hence O(n⁶(log B)³) bit operations with classical arithmetic; the proof counts the passes, the cost of each pass, and bounds every number via (1.27)–(1.36).
The analysis remains valid when L ⊂ ℤ^n is replaced by integrality of all inner products; for rational inner products clear denominators first.

nodes.title: Lengths of a reduced basis against its Gram–Schmidt vectors (1.7)
nodes.statement: For an LLL-reduced family b : Fin n → E (δ = 3/4) and indices 0 ≤ j ≤ i < n, ‖b_j‖² ≤ 2^i·‖b*_i‖².
hypotheses: Zero-based form of the source's |b_j|² ≤ 2^{i−1}|b*_i|² for 1 ≤ j ≤ i ≤ n.
proofSteps: ‖b_i‖² = ‖b*_i‖² + Σ_{j<i} μ_{ij}²‖b*_j‖² ≤ ‖b*_i‖² + (1/4)Σ_{j<i} 2^{i−j}‖b*_i‖² = (2^{i−1} + 1/2)‖b*_i‖² ≤ 2^i‖b*_i‖², using the parent growth bound ‖b*_j‖² ≤ 2^{i−j}‖b*_i‖².
For j ≤ i combine ‖b_j‖² ≤ 2^j‖b*_j‖² with ‖b*_j‖² ≤ 2^{i−j}‖b*_i‖².
acceptance: For the reduced basis ((1,0),(1/2,1)): ‖b_1‖² = 5/4 ≤ 2·1.
For i = 0 the statement is ‖b_0‖² ≤ ‖b*_0‖², an equality.

sources.locator: Proposition (1.6), (1.7) and its proof, reprint folio 29 (PDF p. 3)
sources.match: From (1.4) and (1.5) the orthogonalised lengths grow by at most a factor two per step, and expanding |b_i|² through (1.2) gives |b_j|² ≤ 2^{i−1}|b*_i|² for j ≤ i.

nodes.title: Orthogonality defect of a reduced basis (1.8)
nodes.statement: Let b be an LLL-reduced basis of a lattice L in E, of rank n, and write covol(L) = ∏_i ‖b*_i‖ = (det Gram(b))^{1/2}, which is ZLattice.covolume of L in its real span. Then covol(L) ≤ ∏_i ‖b_i‖ ≤ 2^{n(n−1)/4}·covol(L). The left inequality (Hadamard, (1.10)) holds for every basis.
hypotheses: For a full lattice in E, covol(L) is Mathlib's ZLattice.covolume (GN.0/covolume-square-gram).
proofSteps: covol(L)² = d_n = ∏‖b*_i‖² (parent prefix Gram product) and ‖b*_i‖ ≤ ‖b_i‖ give the left inequality (equivalently GN.0's Hadamard inequality).
lll-basis-length-growth with j = i gives ‖b_i‖ ≤ 2^{i/2}‖b*_i‖; multiply over i to get the factor 2^{n(n−1)/4}.
acceptance: For an orthogonal basis the left inequality is an equality.

sources.locator: Proposition (1.6), (1.8), (1.10) and the proof, reprint folios 29–30 (PDF pp. 3–4)
sources.match: d(L) is the product of the |b*_i|; with |b*_i| ≤ |b_i| ≤ 2^{(i−1)/2}|b*_i| this gives (1.8); the remark (1.10) notes the lower bound is Hadamard's inequality for any basis.

nodes.title: First vector against the covolume (1.9)
nodes.statement: For n ≥ 1 and an LLL-reduced basis b of a rank-n lattice L, ‖b_0‖ ≤ 2^{(n−1)/4}·covol(L)^{1/n}.
hypotheses: Positive rank is needed for the n-th root.
proofSteps: Take j = 0 in lll-basis-length-growth: ‖b_0‖² ≤ 2^i‖b*_i‖² for every i.
Multiply over i: ‖b_0‖^{2n} ≤ 2^{n(n−1)/2}∏‖b*_i‖² = 2^{n(n−1)/2}covol(L)².
acceptance: For ℤ² with the standard basis: 1 ≤ 2^{1/4}.
Combined with lll-short-vector-factor this bounds the first vector both by the minimum and by the covolume.

sources.locator: Proposition (1.6), (1.9) and its proof, reprint folio 29 (PDF p. 3)
sources.match: Putting j = 1 in (1.7) and taking the product over i gives |b_1| ≤ 2^{(n−1)/4}d(L)^{1/n}.

nodes.title: Reduced bases against independent lattice vectors (1.12)
nodes.statement: Let b be an LLL-reduced basis of a rank-n lattice L and x_0, …, x_{t−1} ∈ L linearly independent. Then ‖b_j‖² ≤ 2^{n−1}·max_l ‖x_l‖² for every j < t. The factor 2^{n−1} may be replaced by the certificate constant max{‖b_j‖²/‖b*_i‖² : j ≤ i < n}, and in the short-vector bound by max_i ‖b_0‖²/‖b*_i‖² (Remark (1.14)).
hypotheses: The constants of (1.14) are computable from the exact Gram–Schmidt data of the output.
proofSteps: Write x_l = Σ r_{il} b_i with r_{il} ∈ ℤ and let i(l) be the largest index with r_{i(l),l} ≠ 0; as in (1.11), ‖x_l‖² ≥ ‖b*_{i(l)}‖² ((1.13)).
Order the x_l with i(0) ≤ ⋯ ≤ i(t−1); linear independence forces j ≤ i(j).
Then ‖b_j‖² ≤ 2^{i(j)}‖b*_{i(j)}‖² ≤ 2^{n−1}‖x_j‖² by lll-basis-length-growth; keeping the ratio ‖b_j‖²/‖b*_{i(j)}‖² instead of 2^{i(j)} gives (1.14).
acceptance: With t = 1 the statement is the parent short-vector bound.
For ℤ² with the standard basis and x = ((1,1),(1,−1)), max‖x_l‖² = 2 bounds ‖b_0‖², ‖b_1‖² ≤ 2·2.

sources.locator: Proposition (1.12), (1.13), its proof and Remark (1.14), reprint folio 30 (PDF p. 4)
sources.match: For linearly independent x_1, …, x_t in L, |b_j|² ≤ 2^{n−1} max|x_l|² for j ≤ t, proved by ordering the x_l by their largest nonzero coordinate; (1.14) replaces 2^{n−1} by the observed ratios.

nodes.title: A reduced basis approximates the successive minima
nodes.statement: Let L be a full lattice in an n-dimensional real inner-product space E, b an LLL-reduced basis of L, and λ_i (0 ≤ i < n) the successive minima of L with respect to the closed unit ball (GN.1/successive-minimum, zero-based). Then 2^{−i}·λ_i² ≤ ‖b_i‖² ≤ 2^{n−1}·λ_i². In particular ∏_i λ_i ≤ ∏_i ‖b_i‖ ≤ 2^{n(n−1)/4}·covol(L).
hypotheses: The source's minima are minima of |·|², i.e. our λ_i²; its index i is our i + 1.
proofSteps: Upper bound: GN.1 gives independent x_0, …, x_i ∈ L with ‖x_l‖ = λ_l ≤ λ_i; apply lll-independent-family-bound with t = i + 1 and j = i.
Lower bound: b_0, …, b_i are independent, so λ_i ≤ max_{j ≤ i}‖b_j‖, and ‖b_j‖² ≤ 2^i‖b*_i‖² ≤ 2^i‖b_i‖² by lll-basis-length-growth.
The product statement multiplies the upper bounds of the λ_i ≤ ‖b_{(i)}‖ after sorting, together with lll-orthogonality-defect.
acceptance: For ℤ^n with the standard basis all λ_i = 1 and ‖b_i‖ = 1.

sources.match: With λ_i the successive minima of |·|² on L, (1.7) and (1.12) give 2^{1−i}λ_i ≤ |b_i|² ≤ 2^{n−1}λ_i, so |b_i|² approximates λ_i.

nodes.title: A reduced basis extending a prescribed primitive short vector
nodes.statement: Let Λ be a full lattice in a real inner-product space E of dimension n ≥ 1, A ≥ 1, and u ∈ Λ primitive with ‖u‖ ≤ A·λ_0(Λ) (λ_0 the first minimum for the unit ball). Write V_{i−1} = span_ℝ(b_0, …, b_{i−1}), with V_{−1} = 0. There is a ℤ-basis b_0 = u, b_1, …, b_{n−1} of Λ such that (i) b_0, …, b_{i−1} is a ℤ-basis of Λ ∩ V_{i−1} for every i; (ii) for every 0 ≤ i < n and every w ∈ Λ outside V_{i−1}, ‖b_i‖ ≤ c_i·‖w‖, where c_0 = A and c_i = 1 + (1/2)·Σ_{j<i} c_j for i ≥ 1, so that c_i = (3/2)^{i−1}(1 + A/2) for i ≥ 1 and c_i = (3/2)^i when A = 1; (iii) ‖b_1‖ ≤ ‖b_2‖ ≤ ⋯ ≤ ‖b_{n−1}‖, and when A = 1 also ‖b_0‖ ≤ ‖b_1‖, so that the whole basis is nondecreasing in length. Such a basis is obtained greedily: for i ≥ 1, b_i is a shortest vector of Λ whose class in the free quotient Λ/(Λ ∩ V_{i−1}) is primitive.
hypotheses: For general A the prescribed b_0 = u may be longer than b_1 (A = 3, u = (2,1) in ℤ²), so (iii) starts at b_1. The ordering comes from the greedy choice, not from Minkowski reduction, which BSTTTZ cite (Siegel, Lectures X §6) and which is not used here.
For lattice vectors, lying outside span_ℝ(b_0, …, b_{i−1}) is the same as lying outside its ℚ-span, since b_0, …, b_{i−1} is primitive.
proofSteps: Induction on i, keeping L_i = Λ ∩ V_{i−1} = span_ℤ(b_0, …, b_{i−1}); L_i is saturated, so Λ/L_i is a free ℤ-module of rank n − i. For i = 1, primitivity of u gives Λ ∩ ℝu = ℤu (TauCeti.IsPrimitive), and ‖u‖ ≤ Aλ_0 ≤ A‖w‖ for every nonzero w ∈ Λ is (ii) at i = 0.

Step i ≥ 1: Λ/L_i ≠ 0, so some vector of Λ has primitive class there, and a ball meets the closed discrete subgroup Λ in finitely many points (Metric.finite_isBounded_inter_isClosed), so a shortest vector b_i with primitive class exists. The image of Λ ∩ (V_{i−1} + ℝb_i) in Λ/L_i is a saturated rank-one subgroup containing the primitive class of b_i, hence equal to ℤ·[b_i]; this is (i) for i + 1, and at i = n the basis of Λ is complete (TauCeti.IsPrimitive.exists_basis, GN.0/prescribed-primitive-basis).

(ii): let w ∈ Λ ∖ V_{i−1} and π the orthogonal projection onto V_{i−1}^⊥. The class of w in Λ/L_i is d·p with d ≥ 1 and p primitive (TauCeti.exists_eq_zsmul_isPrimitive), so a lift w′ of p has π(w′) = π(w)/d. Write w′ − π(w′) = Σ_{j<i} t_j b_j and put u′ = w′ − Σ_{j<i} round(t_j) b_j (abs_sub_round). Then u′ has primitive class, so ‖b_i‖ ≤ ‖u′‖ ≤ ‖π(w)‖/d + (1/2)Σ_{j<i}‖b_j‖ ≤ ‖w‖ + (1/2)Σ_{j<i}‖b_j‖.
Since w ∉ V_{j−1} ⊆ V_{i−1} for j < i, induction gives ‖b_j‖ ≤ c_j‖w‖, hence ‖b_i‖ ≤ (1 + (1/2)Σ_{j<i}c_j)‖w‖ = c_i‖w‖.

(iii): for i ≥ 1 the class of b_{i+1} in Λ/L_{i+1} is primitive, hence so is its class in Λ/L_i (pull a functional back along Λ/L_i → Λ/L_{i+1}); so b_{i+1} was a candidate at step i and ‖b_i‖ ≤ ‖b_{i+1}‖. For A = 1, ‖b_0‖ = ‖u‖ ≤ λ_0 ≤ ‖b_1‖.
Evertse's projection-and-lift lemmas give the same saturation and lifting steps for the shortest-vector start A = 1.
acceptance: For Λ = ℤ², u = (1,0), A = 1: c_1 = 3/2, the greedy choice is b_1 = ±(0,1), ‖b_1‖ = 1 ≤ (3/2)‖w‖ for every w ∉ ℝu, and ‖b_0‖ ≤ ‖b_1‖.
For n = 1 the basis is (u) and the only condition is ‖u‖ ≤ Aλ_0.

With A = 3 and u = (2,1) in ℤ² (primitive, ‖u‖ = √5 ≤ 3·1), c_1 = 5/2; the class of (x, y) modulo ℤu is read off by x − 2y, the shortest vector of class ±1 is b_1 = ±(1,0), and ‖b_1‖ = 1 ≤ (5/2)‖w‖ for every w ∉ ℝu; here ‖b_0‖ = √5 > ‖b_1‖, which is why (iii) starts at b_1 when A > 1.
u = 2 in Λ = ℤ is not primitive, and no basis of ℤ begins with it.

sources.match: The paper uses a reduced basis of O_K beginning with 1, nondecreasing in length, whose i-th vector is bounded by a constant times any lattice vector outside the span of the previous ones, with product comparable to √|Disc K|, citing Siegel's Lectures X §6; this node is the generic lattice statement with explicit constants, the number-field trace metric staying with the downstream owner.

The basis is built by starting from a shortest vector, projecting orthogonally to it, and lifting a basis of the projected lattice back with controlled length; the same saturation and rounding steps drive the induction here.

nodes.title: Product of the primitive-prefix basis against the covolume
nodes.statement: For Λ, A, u and the basis b of primitive-prefix-reduced-basis, with λ_0 ≤ ⋯ ≤ λ_{n−1} the successive minima of Λ for the closed unit ball and v_n > 0 the volume of the unit ball of E: ‖b_i‖ ≤ c_i·λ_i for every i, and covol(Λ) ≤ ∏_i ‖b_i‖ ≤ (∏_i c_i)·(2^n/v_n)·covol(Λ).
hypotheses: covol(Λ) is Mathlib's ZLattice.covolume for the canonical volume of E.
proofSteps: Among the GN.1 minimum witnesses x_0, …, x_i (‖x_l‖ = λ_l ≤ λ_i), at least one lies outside the i-dimensional space span_ℝ(b_0, …, b_{i−1}); apply the bound of primitive-prefix-reduced-basis to it.

nodes.title: Exact quadratic completion of a rational symmetric matrix
nodes.statement: For a symmetric G ∈ ℚ^{n×n}, the quadratic completion consists of pivots q_ii and multipliers q_ij (i < j) produced by symmetric Gaussian elimination: q_00 = G_00, q_0j = G_0j/q_00, and inductively the same on the Schur complement of the processed rows. It is defined when every pivot is nonzero, and then xᵀGx = Σ_i q_ii·(x_i + Σ_{j>i} q_ij x_j)² for all x ∈ ℚ^n; equivalently G = Uᵀ·diag(q)·U with U upper unitriangular and U_ij = q_ij. All pivots are positive if and only if G is positive definite, and then det G = ∏_i q_ii. After casting to ℝ the completion of a positive definite G is Mathlib's LDL decomposition: q_ii = LDL.diagEntries i and U = (LDL.lower)ᵀ; Tau Ceti's cholesky factor is Uᵀ·diag(q_ii^{1/2}).
hypotheses: Zero-based indices; the empty matrix has no pivots and is positive definite.
Arithmetic is exact over ℚ; no square root is taken. A nonpositive pivot stops the elimination and certifies that G is not positive definite.
proofSteps: Gaussian elimination on the first row and column writes xᵀGx = q_00(x_0 + Σ_{j>0} q_0j x_j)² + x′ᵀSx′ with S the Schur complement; induct on n.
Positivity of all pivots is equivalent to positive definiteness by Sylvester's criterion in the form d_k = ∏_{i<k} q_ii for the leading minors d_k, together with the displayed sum of squares.

Uniqueness of a factorisation Uᵀ D U with U unit upper triangular and D diagonal invertible identifies the cast completion with LDL.lower and LDL.diagEntries, whose product formula is LDL.lower_conj_diag; cholesky_mul_transpose gives the Cholesky comparison.
acceptance: For G = [[2,1],[1,2]] the pivots are 2 and 3/2 with q_01 = 1/2, and 2·(3/2) = 3 = det G.
For G = [[1,2],[2,1]] the second pivot is −3, so G is not positive definite (x = (1,−1) gives −2).

nodes.statement: For a linearly independent family b : Fin n → E in a real inner-product space with Gram matrix G (G_ij = ⟨b_i, b_j⟩), the quadratic completion of G has pivots q_ii = ‖b*_i‖² and multipliers q_ij = μ_{ji} for i < j: xᵀGx = Σ_i ‖b*_i‖²·(x_i + Σ_{j>i} μ_{ji} x_j)². For an LLL-reduced b this gives q_ii ≥ 2^{−i}‖b_0‖².
hypotheses: G is real here; when G is rational the statement holds in ℚ.
proofSteps: Expand Σ_j x_j b_j = Σ_i (x_i + Σ_{j>i} μ_{ji} x_j) b*_i using b_j = b*_j + Σ_{i<j} μ_{ji} b*_i, and use orthogonality of the b*_i.
A factorisation Uᵀ·diag(q)·U with U unit upper triangular and q positive is unique, so this is the completion.
The LLL bound is the parent growth lemma with j = 0.

nodes.title: Fincke–Pohst enumeration of lattice points in an ellipsoid
nodes.statement: Input: n ≥ 1, a symmetric G ∈ ℚ^{n×n} with positive quadratic-completion pivots, a centre t ∈ ℚ^n and a bound R ∈ ℚ. Put T_{n−1} = R. For k = n − 1, …, 0, given x_{k+1}, …, x_{n−1}, put U_k = Σ_{j>k} q_kj (x_j − t_j), let x_k run over all integers with q_kk·(x_k − t_k + U_k)² ≤ T_k (a finite interval of integers, decided by exact rational comparison), and put T_{k−1} = T_k − q_kk·(x_k − t_k + U_k)². fpEnumeration G t R ⊂ ℤ^n is the finite set of completed vectors x. Boundary points are included, both signs are produced, and for t = 0 and R ≥ 0 the zero vector is included. If R < 0 the set is empty.
hypotheses: The input bound R is exact; a consumer that needs a safety margin enlarges R explicitly and keeps the excess vectors.

The algorithm as de Weger gives it (Figure 2, after Fincke–Pohst (2.8)) stops when it reaches the zero vector, so it lists one vector of each pair ±x and omits 0; this construction lists the whole set, as the completeness theorem requires.

As a total function on symmetric rational matrices, fpEnumeration G t R is ∅ when a pivot of the quadratic completion of G vanishes or is negative; every statement about the enumeration assumes positive pivots unless it says otherwise.
proofSteps: The completion identity makes the partial sums Σ_{i≥k} q_ii(x_i − t_i + U_i)² nondecreasing as k decreases, so each level is a bounded set of integers.
Recursion on k with finite levels gives a finite set; its elements are exactly the leaves.
The integer interval at level k is found by comparing squares of rationals, never by taking square roots.
acceptance: Output depends only on the quadratic form: replacing G by UᵀGU and t by U⁻¹t for U ∈ GL_n(ℤ) maps the output by U⁻¹.

sources.match: All lattice points within a given distance of the origin, or of a non-lattice point after translation, are found by bounding the coordinates one at a time from the quadratic completion, from the last coordinate down, backtracking when a level is exhausted (Fincke–Pohst (2.8), (2.12)).

nodes.title: Soundness and completeness of the Fincke–Pohst enumeration
nodes.statement: Let G ∈ ℚ^{n×n} be symmetric with positive pivots, t ∈ ℚ^n and R ∈ ℚ. For every x ∈ ℤ^n: x ∈ fpEnumeration G t R ⟺ (x − t)ᵀG(x − t) ≤ R. Lattice form: if b is a basis of a lattice L ⊂ E with Gram matrix G and y = Σ_i t_i b_i, then {v ∈ L : ‖v − y‖² ≤ R} = {Σ_i x_i b_i : x ∈ fpEnumeration G t R}. Consequently an empty output certifies ‖v − y‖² > R for all v ∈ L, and for t = 0 an output {0} certifies ‖v‖² > R for every nonzero v ∈ L.
hypotheses: A rational Gram matrix is needed for exact decisions; real Gram matrices go through reduction-transfer-under-comparison.
proofSteps: (⇐) If (x − t)ᵀG(x − t) ≤ R, the completion identity bounds every tail partial sum by R, so at each level x_k lies in the scanned interval for its own tail; by downward induction the tail is produced.
(⇒) A produced x has T_{−1} = R − Σ_i q_ii(x_i − t_i + U_i)² ≥ 0, which is (x − t)ᵀG(x − t) ≤ R.
Lattice form: ‖Σ x_i b_i − y‖² = (x − t)ᵀG(x − t), and x ↦ Σ x_i b_i is a bijection ℤ^n → L.
acceptance: For G = [[2,1],[1,2]] and R = 2 the seven listed vectors are exactly the solutions of 2x² + 2xy + 2y² ≤ 2.
With t = 0 and R just below the squared minimum the output is {0}.

nodes.title: Counting lattice points in an ellipsoid from a reduced basis
nodes.statement: For G ∈ ℚ^{n×n} (or ℝ^{n×n}) symmetric with positive pivots q_ii, t ∈ ℝ^n and R ≥ 0: #{x ∈ ℤ^n : (x − t)ᵀG(x − t) ≤ R} ≤ ∏_{i<n} (1 + 2·(R/q_ii)^{1/2}). If b is an LLL-reduced basis of a full lattice L in E and y ∈ E, then #{v ∈ L : ‖v − y‖² ≤ R} ≤ ∏_{i<n} (1 + 2^{1+i/2}·R^{1/2}/‖b_0‖) ≤ ∏_{i<n} (1 + 2^{1+i/2}·R^{1/2}/λ_0(L)).
hypotheses: λ_0(L) is the first successive minimum (the length of a shortest nonzero vector).
The bound is a count, not an asymptotic; it includes the boundary.
proofSteps: At level k the admissible x_k form the integers of an interval of length 2(T_k/q_kk)^{1/2} ≤ 2(R/q_kk)^{1/2}, hence at most 1 + 2(R/q_kk)^{1/2} values; multiply over the levels.
For a Gram matrix q_ii = ‖b*_i‖² (quadratic-completion-gram-schmidt), and for an LLL-reduced basis ‖b*_i‖² ≥ 2^{−i}‖b_0‖² ≥ 2^{−i}λ_0².
acceptance: G = I_2, R = 1: the bound is 3·3 = 9 ≥ 5.
For n = 1, G = (q), the count of integers in an interval of length 2(R/q)^{1/2} is at most 1 + 2(R/q)^{1/2}.

nodes.title: Certified representation numbers of a positive definite lattice
nodes.statement: Let L be a positive definite Tau Ceti integral lattice (TauCeti.IntegralLattice with IsPosDef) whose carrier has a ℤ-basis e : Fin n → L, let G = gramMatrix e ∈ ℤ^{n×n}, and let m ∈ ℤ. The map x ↦ Σ_i x_i e_i is a bijection from {x ∈ fpEnumeration G 0 m : xᵀGx = m} onto the shell {v ∈ L : B(v, v) = m}, so the enumeration computes the representation number r_L(m), the cardinality of that shell, exactly. Consequently L represents m exactly when the filtered enumeration is nonempty, and the minimum of B(v, v) over nonzero v ∈ L is the least m ≥ 1 for which it is nonempty, found by the single enumeration at R = G_00. The shells, their finiteness, r_L itself, r_L(m) = 0 for m < 0, r_L(0) = 1 and the minimum are not planned here: they are TauCetiRoadmap IntegralLattices milestones 2A–2B, built on current Tau Ceti main after the pin (IntegralLattice.IsPosDef.finite_vectorsOfNorm, representationNumber, IsPosSemidef.representationNumber_eq_zero_of_neg, representationNumber_zero_of_anisotropic, minimum); this node adds only their certified computation.
hypotheses: The norm is B(v, v), Tau Ceti's IntegralLattice.norm; a quadratic form q = B/2 halves every value.

Positive definiteness of G over ℚ follows from IsPosDef: map_gramMatrix identifies the cast of G with the matrix of the ambient form in the ℚ-basis extending e, and LinearMap.BilinForm.posDef_toQuadraticMap_iff_matrix compares positive definiteness of a quadratic map with that of its matrix, so the completion has positive pivots. (isPosDef_ofGramMatrix_iff covers only lattices built by ofGramMatrix.)
These are global finite tests; local representation densities over ℤ_p are the separate GN.2–GN.3 owners.
proofSteps: Use the bijection ℤ^n ≃ L given by e and the identity B(Σ x_i e_i, Σ x_i e_i) = xᵀGx.
Completeness of the enumeration at R = m lists every x with xᵀGx ≤ m; filtering by equality gives the shell.
m < 0 gives an empty output; m = 0 gives {0} by positive definiteness; the minimum is attained by e_0 or a shorter vector, all of which the enumeration at R = G_00 lists.
acceptance: For the hexagonal lattice G = [[2,1],[1,2]]: r(2) = 6 and the minimum is 2.
For every positive definite L the filtered enumeration is empty at m = −1 and is {0} at m = 0, matching r_L(−1) = 0 and r_L(0) = 1 on current Tau Ceti main.

nodes.title: Two-sided comparison of a Gram matrix with a rational model
nodes.statement: For a real symmetric G ∈ ℝ^{n×n}, a rational symmetric G̃ ∈ ℚ^{n×n} and a rational ε with 0 ≤ ε < 1, GramComparison G G̃ ε holds when (1 − ε)·xᵀG̃x ≤ xᵀGx ≤ (1 + ε)·xᵀG̃x for all x ∈ ℝ^n, i.e. G − (1 − ε)G̃ and (1 + ε)G̃ − G are positive semidefinite. It is the hypothesis under which an exact rational reduction or enumeration is transferred to an irrational metric.
hypotheses: The comparison is in the Loewner order of quadratic forms, not entrywise.
ε < 1 makes G positive definite exactly when G̃ is.
proofSteps: Define the predicate by the two inequalities for all real x.
Derive the bilinear bound |xᵀ(G − G̃)y| ≤ ε(xᵀG̃x)^{1/2}(yᵀG̃y)^{1/2} by Cauchy–Schwarz for the semidefinite forms εG̃ ± (G − G̃).
Change of basis: GramComparison G G̃ ε implies GramComparison (UᵀGU) (UᵀG̃U) ε for every rational square matrix U (so that UᵀG̃U is again rational), in particular for U ∈ GL_n(ℤ).
acceptance: G = G̃ gives the comparison with ε = 0.
G = diag(1, 2) and G̃ = I admit no ε < 1.

nodes.title: From entrywise enclosures to a Loewner comparison
nodes.statement: Let G ∈ ℝ^{n×n} be symmetric, G̃ ∈ ℚ^{n×n} symmetric, rationals η ≥ 0 and 0 < ε < 1, with |G_ij − G̃_ij| ≤ η for all i, j. If G̃ − (nη/ε)·I_n has positive quadratic-completion pivots, then GramComparison G G̃ ε.
hypotheses: The hypothesis on G̃ is decided exactly in ℚ by the quadratic completion; only the enclosure |G_ij − G̃_ij| ≤ η concerns the real matrix.
proofSteps: |xᵀ(G − G̃)x| ≤ η(Σ_i |x_i|)² ≤ nη‖x‖² by the entrywise bound and Cauchy–Schwarz.
Positive pivots give G̃ − (nη/ε)I positive definite, so nη‖x‖² ≤ ε·xᵀG̃x.
acceptance: n = 1, G = (π), G̃ = (3), η = 1/5, ε = 1/10: 3 − 2 = 1 > 0, so the comparison holds.
If η = 0 the comparison holds for every ε ∈ (0,1) as soon as G̃ is positive definite.

nodes.title: Transfer of the LLL factor and enumeration covers to an irrational metric
nodes.statement: Let b be a basis of a lattice L in E with real Gram matrix G, and GramComparison G G̃ ε with κ = (1 + ε)/(1 − ε). (a) If U ∈ GL_n(ℤ) and the rational form UᵀG̃U is LLL-reduced (for its coordinate basis), then c = b·U is a basis of L with ‖c_0‖² ≤ κ·2^{n−1}·‖x‖² for every nonzero x ∈ L and ‖c_0‖² ≤ κ·2^{(n−1)/2}·covol(L)^{2/n}. (b) For rational t, R ≥ 0 and y = Σ_i t_i b_i: {v ∈ L : ‖v − y‖² ≤ R} ⊆ {Σ_i x_i b_i : x ∈ fpEnumeration G̃ t (R/(1 − ε))}; the excess vectors are kept and filtered by a separate exact or enclosed test.
hypotheses: Reducedness is certified for the rational model only; no claim is made that c is LLL-reduced for G.
proofSteps: (a) The LLL short-vector bound for the rational form gives e_0ᵀUᵀG̃Ue_0 ≤ 2^{n−1}zᵀG̃z for every nonzero integer z; the comparison converts both sides, giving the factor κ.
The covolume bound: lll-first-vector-covolume for UᵀG̃U and det G̃ ≤ (1 − ε)^{−n}·det G by loewner-det-monotone, with det G = covol(L)².
(b) (x − t)ᵀG(x − t) ≤ R implies (x − t)ᵀG̃(x − t) ≤ R/(1 − ε); apply completeness of the enumeration for G̃.
acceptance: With ε = 0 part (a) is the parent original-lattice verification.
For G = diag(1, 11/10), G̃ = I, ε = 1/10 and U = I the bound reads ‖c_0‖² ≤ (11/9)·2·‖x‖².

nodes.title: Determinants are monotone in the Loewner order
nodes.statement: Let A, B ∈ ℝ^{n×n} be symmetric with A positive definite and B positive semidefinite, and xᵀBx ≤ xᵀAx for all x ∈ ℝ^n. Then det B ≤ det A. In particular, if G̃ is positive definite, GramComparison G G̃ ε gives (1 − ε)^n·det G̃ ≤ det G ≤ (1 + ε)^n·det G̃.
hypotheses: Mathlib at the pin has no monotonicity of the determinant in the Loewner order; this lemma supplies it for the transfer theorem.
proofSteps: Write A = L·Lᵀ with L = cholesky A and put C = L^{−1}·B·L^{−ᵀ}, symmetric positive semidefinite with yᵀCy ≤ yᵀy.
Every eigenvalue of C lies in [0, 1] (Rayleigh quotients), so det C = ∏ eigenvalues ≤ 1.
det B = det A·det C ≤ det A; the GramComparison form applies this to (1 − ε)G̃ ≤ G and G ≤ (1 + ε)G̃.
acceptance: A = diag(2, 3), B = diag(1, 3): det B = 3 ≤ 6.
If B = A the inequality is an equality.

sources.match: The determinant of a Hermitian matrix is the product of its eigenvalues, each a Rayleigh quotient; the Cholesky factor reduces the comparison to one with the identity.

nodes.title: The Euclidean lattice of a fractional ideal
nodes.statement: For a number field K of degree n with r₁ real and r₂ complex places and an invertible fractional ideal I of 𝓞_K, euclideanIdealLattice K I is the ℤ-lattice ZLattice.comap ℝ (mixedEmbedding.idealLattice K I) (euclidean.toMixed K) in Mathlib's Euclidean mixed space ℝ^{r₁} × ℂ^{r₂}, i.e. the image of I under ι = (toMixed)⁻¹ ∘ mixedEmbedding. It is discrete and full of rank n, ‖ι(a)‖² = Σ_{w real} w(a)² + Σ_{w complex} w(a)² (each place counted once), and its covolume is absNorm(I)·2^{−r₂}·√|disc K|. For I = 𝓞_K it is Mathlib's euclidean.integerLattice.
hypotheses: The metric counts each complex place once; the trace form T2(a) = Σ_σ |σ(a)|² counts it twice, so ‖ι(a)‖² ≤ T2(a) ≤ 2‖ι(a)‖², with equality on the left for totally real K.
No new metric is introduced: the trace metric on the mixed space belongs to the class-group torsion roadmap that imports this lattice.
proofSteps: Define the lattice by ZLattice.comap along the continuous linear equivalence toMixed; discreteness and fullness transfer.
The norm formula is the ℓ² norm of the Euclidean mixed space evaluated on the mixed embedding.
The covolume is unchanged by comap along a volume-preserving equivalence (covolume_comap with volumePreserving_toMixed), and Mathlib computes the covolume of idealLattice.
acceptance: For K = ℚ(i), I = 𝓞_K the lattice is ℤ[i] ⊂ ℂ with covolume 2^{−1}·√4 = 1.
For K = ℚ, I = (2) the lattice is 2ℤ ⊂ ℝ with covolume 2.

sources.match: Mathlib provides the Euclidean mixed space with its volume-preserving identification with the mixed space, the integer lattice there, and the covolume of the ideal lattice.

K ⊗ ℝ ≅ ℝ^{r₁} × ℂ^{r₂} is made Euclidean by a positive definite quadratic form, and small elements are those of small norm; Belabas uses T2, which differs from Mathlib's ℓ² structure only on complex coordinates.

nodes.title: House and norm bounded by the Euclidean length
nodes.statement: For a number field K of degree n ≥ 1 and α ∈ K: house(α) ≤ ‖ι(α)‖, and |N_{K/ℚ}(α)|^{2/n} ≤ (2/n)·‖ι(α)‖²; when K is totally real, |N_{K/ℚ}(α)|^{2/n} ≤ (1/n)·‖ι(α)‖².
hypotheses: ‖ι(α)‖ is the Euclidean mixed-space norm of ideal-euclidean-lattice; house is Mathlib's NumberField.house.
proofSteps: house(α) = max_w w(α) and each place occurs once in ‖ι(α)‖², so house(α)² ≤ ‖ι(α)‖².

|N(α)| = ∏_w w(α)^{mult w} with Σ_w mult w = n; weighted AM–GM with weights mult(w)/n on the values w(α)² gives |N(α)|^{2/n} ≤ (1/n)Σ_w mult(w)·w(α)² ≤ (2/n)‖ι(α)‖², and the factor 2 disappears when every place is real.

sources.match: By the arithmetic–geometric mean inequality |N x|^{2/n} ≤ T2(x)/n, so an element with small coordinates in a T2-reduced basis has small norm.
The norm is the weighted product over infinite places, the weights sum to the degree, and the house is the largest conjugate.

nodes.title: Height of an algebraic integer from its house
nodes.statement: For a number field K of degree n and α ∈ 𝓞_K: logHeight₁(α) ≤ n·log⁺ house(α) ≤ (n/2)·log⁺ ‖ι(α)‖², where logHeight₁ is Mathlib's (unnormalised) logarithmic Weil height on K.
hypotheses: Moved down from DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.4/log-height-of-algebraic-integer-bound, which states the first inequality; that node imports this one.
proofSteps: By logHeight₁_eq, logHeight₁(α) = Σ_w mult(w)·log⁺ w(α) + Σᶠ_v log⁺ v(α).
At finite places v(α) ≤ 1 for an algebraic integer, so the second sum vanishes.
w(α) ≤ house(α) and Σ_w mult(w) = n give the first inequality; house(α)² ≤ ‖ι(α)‖² gives the second.
acceptance: α = 2 ∈ ℤ ⊂ ℚ: logHeight₁(2) = log 2 = 1·log⁺ 2.
A root of unity has house 1 and height 0.

sources.match: The height is the weighted sum of log⁺ of the absolute values over all places, and integral elements have finite absolute values at most one.
Small T2 controls the archimedean size of an integral element, which is what the height of an algebraic integer measures.

nodes.title: A certified short element of an ideal
nodes.statement: Let K have degree n with r₂ complex places, I an invertible fractional ideal with ℤ-basis (β_j), G the real Gram matrix of ι(β_j) in the Euclidean mixed space, G̃ rational with GramComparison G G̃ ε, κ = (1 + ε)/(1 − ε), and U ∈ GL_n(ℤ) with UᵀG̃U LLL-reduced. Put α = Σ_j U_{j0} β_j. Then α ∈ I, α ≠ 0, and (i) ‖ι(α)‖² ≤ κ·2^{n−1}·‖ι(β)‖² for every nonzero β ∈ I; (ii) ‖ι(α)‖² ≤ κ·2^{(n−1)/2}·(absNorm(I)·2^{−r₂}·√|disc K|)^{2/n}; (iii) |N_{K/ℚ}(α)| ≤ (2κ/n)^{n/2}·2^{n(n−1)/4}·2^{−r₂}·√|disc K|·absNorm(I); (iv) house(α) ≤ ‖ι(α)‖, and if I ⊆ 𝓞_K then logHeight₁(α) ≤ (n/2)·log⁺(κ·2^{(n−1)/2}·(absNorm(I)·2^{−r₂}·√|disc K|)^{2/n}).
hypotheses: All data (β, G̃, ε, U) are exact; the only real input is the enclosure behind GramComparison, typically produced by entrywise-enclosure-comparison.
For totally real K one may take G̃ = G = (Tr(β_iβ_j)), ε = 0, and the factor 2κ/n in (iii) improves to 1/n.
proofSteps: α ∈ I and α ≠ 0 because U is unimodular and (β_j) is a basis of I.
(i) and (ii) are reduction-transfer-under-comparison for the lattice euclideanIdealLattice K I, with its covolume.
(iii) and (iv) follow from (ii) by euclidean-house-norm-bounds and integral-log-height-le-house.
acceptance: K = ℚ(i), I = (1 + i) with basis (1 + i, 2), exact Gram [[2,2],[2,4]], ε = 0: LLL returns α = ±(1 + i) or ±(1 − i) up to units, and |N(α)| = 2 ≤ (2/2)·2^{1/2}·2^{−1}·2·2.
For K = ℚ, n = 1, the statement says α generates I and |α| = absNorm(I).

sources.match: LLL bounds for a reduced basis of an ideal lattice for T2, the AM–GM bound for the norm, and the transfer to an integral approximation of T2.
The first vector of a reduced basis is bounded by the covolume and by every nonzero lattice vector.

nodes.title: Certified small integral representatives of ideal classes
nodes.statement: Let I be a nonzero integral ideal of 𝓞_K and α ∈ I the element of ideal-short-element for I. Then J = α·I^{−1} is an integral ideal in the class of I^{−1} with absNorm(J) = |N_{K/ℚ}(α)|/absNorm(I) ≤ (2κ/n)^{n/2}·2^{n(n−1)/4}·2^{−r₂}·√|disc K|. Applied to a representative of each class of the inverse, this lists, with exact certificates, an integral ideal of bounded norm in every class; the constant is weaker than Minkowski's bound of NumberField.exists_ideal_in_class_of_norm_le.
hypotheses: The data certifying J are those of ideal-short-element; finiteness of the class group itself is Mathlib's.
proofSteps: α ∈ I gives (α) ⊆ I, hence J = (α)I^{−1} ⊆ 𝓞_K, and J is in the class of I^{−1}.
absNorm is multiplicative and absNorm((α)) = |N(α)|; divide (iii) of ideal-short-element by absNorm(I).
This is the step of Mathlib's proof of exists_ideal_in_class_of_norm_le with the Minkowski element replaced by the certified LLL element.
acceptance: For K = ℚ(√−5) (n = 2, r₂ = 1, |disc| = 20, ε = 0) the bound is (2/2)·2^{1/2}·2^{−1}·√20 ≈ 3.16, so every class has an integral representative of norm at most 3; the nontrivial class is represented by (2, 1 + √−5) of norm 2.
For K = ℚ the bound is 1 and J = (1).

sources.match: The class-group bound passes from a small element of an ideal to an integral ideal of the inverse class with norm |N(α)|/absNorm(I).
The AM–GM bound for the norm of a small element.

nodes.title: Certified simultaneous Diophantine approximation (1.39)
nodes.statement: Given n ≥ 1, rationals α_1, …, α_n and a rational ε with 0 < ε < 1, LLL reduction of the lattice of rank n + 1 spanned by the columns of the matrix with identity block I_n, last column (−α_1, …, −α_n, 2^{−n(n+1)/4}ε^{n+1})ᵀ and zero last row otherwise, produces integers p_1, …, p_n, q with |p_i − qα_i| ≤ ε for all i and 1 ≤ q ≤ 2^{n(n+1)/4}ε^{−n}, in a number of operations polynomial in the input size, together with the unimodular certificate.
hypotheses: All inner products of the columns are rational (the last diagonal entry squares to 2^{−n(n+1)/2}ε^{2n+2}), so the exact reduction applies after clearing denominators.
This is the algorithmic counterpart of Dirichlet's theorem with a weaker constant; Diophantine reductions of linear forms stay with EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.1.
proofSteps: The lattice has covolume 2^{−n(n+1)/4}ε^{n+1}, so (1.9) in rank n + 1 gives ‖b_0‖ ≤ 2^{n/4}·(2^{−n(n+1)/4}ε^{n+1})^{1/(n+1)} = ε.
Writing b_0 = (p_1 − qα_1, …, p_n − qα_n, q·2^{−n(n+1)/4}ε^{n+1}) gives |p_i − qα_i| ≤ ε and |q| ≤ 2^{n(n+1)/4}ε^{−n}.
ε < 1 and b_0 ≠ 0 force q ≠ 0; replace b_0 by −b_0 if necessary.
Polynomial time is lll-arithmetic-complexity for the scaled integral lattice.
acceptance: If every α_i is an integer the vector with q = 1, p_i = α_i is admissible.

sources.locator: Proposition (1.39) and its proof, reprint folios 36–37 (PDF pp. 10–11)
sources.match: A polynomial-time algorithm finds p_i, q with |p_i − qα_i| ≤ ε and 1 ≤ q ≤ 2^{n(n+1)/4}ε^{−n}, by applying (1.9) to the stated lattice of rank n + 1.

nodes.title: LLL-reduced bases are reduced in the sense of Siegel sets
nodes.statement: Let b be an LLL-reduced basis (δ = 3/4) of a rank-n lattice in a real inner-product space, with Gram matrix B_ij = ⟨b_i, b_j⟩. Then |B_ij| ≤ 2^{i+1}·B_ii for all i, j; B_ii ≤ 2^{n−1}·B_jj for i < j; and ∏_i B_ii ≤ 2^{n(n−1)/2}·det B. Consequently B is (e, C_n)-reduced for the standard basis e in the sense of AdelicAlgebraicGroups AA.3 (RealSiegel.IsReduced), with C_n = 2^{n(n−1)/2} + 2^n. For a positive definite form A on ℝ^n and U ∈ GL_n(ℤ) whose columns form an LLL-reduced basis for A (that is, UᵀAU is LLL-reduced), UᵀAU lies in T_{e,C_n}: U is an explicit witness γ for AA.3’s reduction theorem in the form b ↦ γᵀbγ of its suggested RealSiegel.exists_reduced_GLZ; for the action g·b = (g^{−1})ᵀbg^{−1} on forms the moving element is U^{−1}.
hypotheses: All three inequalities are strict once C_n replaces the displayed constants, as AA.3's definition requires.
For a real form, the existence of a reduced basis uses lll-step-termination (b); for a rational form the certificate is computed exactly.
proofSteps: For j ≤ i: ⟨b_i, b_j⟩ = Σ_{l≤j} μ_{il}μ_{jl}‖b*_l‖² (μ_{ll} = 1), so |⟨b_i, b_j⟩| ≤ Σ_{l≤i}‖b*_l‖² ≤ Σ_{l≤i} 2^{i−l}‖b*_i‖² ≤ 2^{i+1}‖b_i‖²; for j > i the same sum stops at l = i.
For i < j, lll-basis-length-growth gives ‖b_i‖² ≤ 2^j‖b*_j‖² ≤ 2^{n−1}‖b_j‖².
The product inequality is the square of lll-orthogonality-defect.
Translate into AA.3's three conditions with the constant C_n; the change of basis is the certificate.
acceptance: For the standard basis of ℤ^n, B = I and every inequality holds with room.

sources.locator: Proposition (1.6) and Remark after it, reprint folio 29 (PDF p. 3)

nodes.title: An LLL certificate places GL_n(ℝ) in a standard Siegel domain
nodes.statement: Let c be an LLL-reduced basis of ℝ^n and C the matrix with columns c_i, with C = Q·D·N where Q is orthogonal, D = diag(‖c*_i‖) and N is upper unitriangular with N_ij = μ_{ji} for i < j. Then |N_ij| ≤ 1/2, ‖c*_{i+1}‖² ≥ (1/2)‖c*_i‖², and |(N^{−1})_ij| ≤ (1/2)(3/2)^{j−i−1} for i < j. Consequently, for g ∈ GL_n(ℝ), let b be the basis formed by the columns of g^{−1} and U an LLL certificate with c = b·U; then γ = U^{−1} ∈ GL_n(ℤ) satisfies γg = v·diag(a)·k with v = N^{−1} upper unitriangular, |v_ij| ≤ u_n := (1/2)(3/2)^{max(n−2,0)}, a_i = ‖c*_i‖^{−1} with a_i/a_{i+1} ≥ 2^{−1/2}, and k = Qᵀ ∈ O(n). That is, γg lies in the standard real Siegel domain Σ_n(u_n, 2^{−1/2}) of AdelicAlgebraicGroups AA.3, an explicit instance of its reduction theorem for GL_n(ℝ).
hypotheses: AA.3's conventions: left action of GL_n(ℤ), coordinates v·diag(a)·k, and gram g = (g^{−1})ᵀg^{−1} the Gram matrix of the columns of g^{−1}.

For irrational g the certificate is produced through a rational model (reduction-transfer-under-comparison) or by the existence statement lll-step-termination (b); for rational g it is computed exactly.
proofSteps: The QR (Gram–Schmidt) factorisation of C has R = D·N with the stated entries, by c_j = Σ_{i≤j} μ_{ji}c*_i.
Size reduction gives |N_ij| ≤ 1/2; size reduction with the Lovász condition gives ‖c*_{i+1}‖² ≥ (3/4 − 1/4)‖c*_i‖².
Back substitution in N·N^{−1} = I bounds the entries of N^{−1} by X_k with X_0 = 1 and X_k ≤ (1/2)Σ_{l<k}X_l, i.e. X_k = (1/2)(3/2)^{k−1}.
(γg)^{−1} = g^{−1}U = C = QDN, so γg = N^{−1}D^{−1}Qᵀ, which has the stated Siegel coordinates.
acceptance: For g = I the certificate is U = I and γg = I = 1·diag(1)·1 lies in Σ_n(u_n, 2^{−1/2}).
For n = 3 the entry (N^{−1})_{02} is μ_{10}μ_{21} − μ_{20}, of absolute value at most 3/4 = u_3.

sources.match: Reduced bases have |μ_ij| ≤ 1/2 and |b*_i|² ≥ (1/2)|b*_{i−1}|², which are the Siegel-set conditions in Iwasawa coordinates.

sourceIssues.printed: The paper says that the length on the ring of integers induced by the conjugate trace pairing equals the sum of the squares of all archimedean absolute values, and identifies it with the usual Euclidean length of the embedding into ℝ^r × ℂ^s (ℂ identified with ℝ²), in which the ring of integers has covolume 2^{−s}·|Disc(K)|^{1/2}.

The two agree only for totally real K; in general |x|_usual² ≤ |x|_trace² ≤ 2|x|_usual², and the covolume 2^{−s}|Disc(K)|^{1/2} is that of the usual length, the trace length giving |Disc(K)|^{1/2}.
